content.text: ▪︎dyslipidemia = abnormality in any serum lipid level
▪︎dx: TC >200, LDL >100, or TG ≥150 mg/dL (= ↑LDL or non-HDL cholest, often w/ ↑TG)
▪︎healthy lipid panel: TC <200, LDL <100, TG <150 mg/dL

▪︎acquired: obesity, nephrotic syndrome, pregnancy, tamoxifen, hypercholest; hereditary: familial chylomicronemia, familial hyperTG, familial combined HLD, dysbetalipoproteinemia (genetic testing if hereditary suspected)
- meds: thiazides, BBs (⍉carvedilol), retinoids, antiretrovirals, cyclosporine,
▪︎hereditary TG: familial chylomicronemia, familial hypertriglyceridemia, dysbetalipoproteinemia, familial combined hyperlipidemia
HTN, DM, FHx of premature ASCVD, cigarette smoke, CKD, obesity
– sedentary lifestyle, diet high in saturated fat + cholesterol
– inflam disorders (ex, RA, SLE, psoriasis, HIV)
▪︎xanthomas: sm yellow/erythematous papules-nodules; MC extensor surfaces + buttocks
•yellow collection of cholest under skin, USU on/peri eyelids
•MC medial eyelids; classic feature of PBC
– arcus cornealis: white/gray opaque ring @ corneal margin (cholest deposits in corneal stroma)
▪︎xanthelasma: soft, yellow, thin plaques; MC on eyelids, neck, trunk, shoulders, axillae; eyelid xanthoma = plane xanthoma on lower eyelid
•lipemia retinalis: cream-colored blood vessels in fundus
▪︎hyperTG: serum TG ≥150 = hyperTG; RF for atherosclerosis + CVD; assoc w/ ⇣HDL, ⇡LDL, insulin resistance, hypercoagulability, hyperviscosity
▪︎dx: fasting TG >200 w/o ↑LDL = hypertriglyceridemia; ↑LDL too = mixed lipoproteinemia
screen traditional RFs & obtain baseline fasting lipid profile for ≥20y,
▪︎universal screen: 9-11yo + again @ 17-21yo; after 21 → reassess CV risk q4-6yrs
if 1+ traditional RF (HTN, obesity, diabetes, etc.)
f/u lipid screening @ 25-30yo for males, 30-35yo for females
start regular lipid screening @ 35yo for males, 45yo for female
▪︎USPSTF: statin for primary prevention in adults 40-75yo w/ ≥1 CV RF + est 10-yr CVD risk ≥10% (RFs: age, cholesterol, obesity, SBP, DM, smoking)
▪︎lifestyle modification (diet, exercise, smoke cessation) + pharm; start pharm based on age, RFs, 10-yr + lifetime risk ⍉strict lab values
▪︎1st-line tx: diet, exercise, lifestyle modification (pharm if refractory)
▪︎statin SEs: nausea, constipation, ⇡AST/ALT (hepatotoxicity), hepatitis, cirrhosis, pancreatitis, cholelithiasis, ⇡CK, rhabdomyolysis, SJS, thrombocytopenia, kidney dysfxn
▪︎high-intensity (⇣LDL ≥50%): atorvastatin 40-80mg, rosuvastatin 20-40mg; moderate-intensity (⇣LDL 30-50%): atorvastatin 10-20mg, rosuvastatin 5-10mg, simvastatin 20-40mg, pravastatin 40-80mg
▪︎statin for TG 150–500; fenofibrate or ezetimibe if statin-⍉tolerant; fish oil adjunct if TG still ⇡ after high-dose statin
▪︎severe TG: fenofibrate 1st-line (safe w/ statin); gemfibrozil + statin → ⇡muscle toxicity → ⍉1st-line
▪︎lifestyle: wt loss, aerobic exercise, glycemic control, ⍉alcohol/sugars/TG-raising meds
▪︎nicotinic acid: ⇣TG 15-25%, worsens glucose tolerance, + statin can be harmful
▪︎omega-3: ⇣TG up to 50%; GI SEs + ⇡LDL limit use
2026 ACC/AHA (PREVENT-ASCVD), adults 30-79 w/ LDL 70-189 w/o DM:
– 10-yr risk <3% (low): moderate-intensity if LDL 160-189 or 30-yr risk ≥10%
– 3-<5% (borderline): moderate-intensity (± coronary artery calcium to decide)
– 40-75yo + DM: moderate-intensity; DM + multiple ASCVD RFs → high-intensity
– >75yo + DM + life expectancy ≥2.5y: moderate-intensity after risk/benefit discussion
– 20-39yo + long-duration DM, albuminuria, eGFR <60, retinopathy, neuropathy, or ABI <0.9: moderate-intensity
– consider statin in select pts: CKD stage 3+, HIV
▪︎goal LDL on statin: <100 (borderline/intermediate); <70 (high; ASCVD not very high risk); <55 (ASCVD very high risk); AACE (2025): <70 for ↑risk/ASCVD
repeat lipid profile 4-12wks after statin initiation/dosage chg
